record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.original_question: Given matrices A, B, and C defining the linear system x'(t) = A x(t) + B u(t), y(t) = C x(t), determine necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a static output-feedback matrix K such that A + B K C is asymptotically stable. This is the classic output-feedback stabilizability problem for systems without full-state access.

evidence.quote: One of the most basic unsolved problems in control theory is the problem of output feedback stabilizability: Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on (A, B, C) under which there exists K such that A + BKC is asymptotically stable.
Conditions for exact stabilizability, however, are unknown.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$, and $C \in \mathbb{R}^{p\times n}$ be given real matrices, defining the linear time-invariant control system
$$\dot{x}(t) = A x(t) + B u(t), \qquad y(t) = C x(t),$$
where $x(t) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $u(t) \in \mathbb{R}^m$, and $y(t) \in \mathbb{R}^p$. A square matrix $M$ is called asymptotically stable (Hurwitz) if every eigenvalue of $M$ has strictly negative real part. The static output-feedback law $u(t) = K y(t)$ with $K \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times p}$ yields the closed-loop dynamics $\dot{x}(t) = (A + BKC) x(t)$.

Problem: Determine verifiable necessary and sufficient conditions on the triple $(A, B, C)$ for the existence of a matrix $K \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times p}$ such that $A + BKC$ is asymptotically stable.
artifact.status_search_result: The static output-feedback stabilization problem is widely regarded as a long-standing open problem in control theory. Various characterizations exist (e.g., via coupled Riccati/Lyapunov equations, bilinear matrix inequalities, or rank conditions), but these are themselves NP-hard or computationally intractable to verify; no tractable necessary and sufficient conditions on $(A,B,C)$ are known. Surveys and recent literature continue to describe the problem as unsolved in this sense.

status_evidence.title: Static Output Feedback Stabilization: A story of people and matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing static output feedback stabilization as a notoriously difficult and largely open problem despite many partial results.
status_evidence.claim: Problem remains open in the sense that no tractable necessary and sufficient conditions are known.

status_evidence.title: A necessary and sufficient condition for output feedback stabilizability
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a necessary and sufficient condition formulated as a coupled matrix equation, which is not computationally tractable.
status_evidence.claim: Known characterizations exist but are not verifiable in polynomial time.
